Okay, so picture this: I’m a bear lurking in a serene corner of Thailand, and this little game shows up. The setup is cute you wander through hand-drawn Thai scenes hunting for hidden cats, then colour the backgrounds in a casual (almost meditative) way. The dev name is Two Cats Games, and yes, there are many cats. 

What works: The visuals are mellow and pleasing, the concept is simple and relaxing (which is nice when I want to be like a bear lying down after a good salmon run). The user reviews show people enjoying the chill hunt-and-colour loop. 
Also the fact you can play solo or in a little local co-op gives it a bit more flexibility.

What doesn’t work so well: It’s very light on depth. If you’re expecting a big narrative, complicated puzzles or a long campaign you’ll underwhelm, kinda like expecting a full feast and getting only a picnic basket. Some minor bugs or interface irritation (menus, screen layout) show up. 

So yeah if you want a mellow time, some hidden-object + colouring fun and you don’t mind that it’s quite casual, this is for you. If you were hoping for something more intense or long-lasting, maybe temper expectations a bit.

Normally I'd be fine recommending these types of games because they're easy for achievement collectors to just add another one to their library, inoffensive, and usually credit the artists in their work. Not every game has to reinvent the wheel. Sadly in this case this game has not credited the artists for this work, and on top of that appears to be using an AI generated music track without declaring so on their steam page, something that's really just dishonest. If it had been declared in the first place, I would not have downloaded this game at all. If this type of game is something that you enjoy, there's much better ones out there.

As with their previous title, this is either not crediting the artists who created the music (the same exact music as last game, btw), or they've used AI music without declaring it. Either way; thumbs down, do not recommend, Steam is flooded with free cat-finding games where the people who made it [i]actually made it[/i]. Go play one of those.

(Oh, and don't be fooled by that "0.5 hours played"; I nipped to the shop in the middle of this one. You'll easily be done finding cats in 5 minutes.)
